A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MemRec and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched across layout changes and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original recommendation experiments on four datasets, together with ablations, architectural comparisons, efficiency measurements, and rationale-quality evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds user-activity, noisy-history, and neighbor-filtering results in Section 3.6 and Appendix G.2.

M1.justification: The curation, synthesis, grounded ranking, and asynchronous propagation procedures remain unchanged. Equations 1–6 and the complete appendix rules and prompts are retained; the new method illustrations explain existing components.

E1.justification: The four datasets and recommendation tasks are retained. Section 3.6 adds a noisy-input scenario through fake-item injection into user histories. Activity-based subgroup analysis partitions an existing test subset.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark tables retain LightGCN, SASRec, P5, Vanilla LLM, iAgent, RecBot, AgentCF, and i2Agent. The new analyses reuse Vanilla LLM and the existing generic-rule ablation; the architectural comparison configurations are also retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds activity stratification, 0–30% history perturbation, and a neighbor-filtering protocol using recency and interaction-overlap thresholds across 15,782 neighbors. Section 3.4 also changes the cost comparison to explicitly focus on online re-ranking, with online and complete-session token accounting distinguished in Table 5. The principal ranking protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 3.6 adds analyses of performance across user-activity groups and resistance to injected noise. Appendix G.2 adds quantitative evidence about filtering irrelevant neighbors, extending the earlier qualitative curation comparison. Existing ablations, sensitivity analyses, rationale evaluation, and the case study remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain significance statements for benchmark comparisons and 95% confidence intervals with paired t-tests for rationale quality. No new repeated-run counts, seed information, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Main ranking and ablation scores are unchanged. New results include a 91.4% relative Hit@1 advantage over Vanilla LLM for low-activity users, Hit@1 of 0.491 under 30% noise, and filtering precision of 0.813 versus 0.861. Efficiency figures also change: Standard total tokens in Table 5 change from approximately 9.7k to 6.8k. These revisions do not establish a same-setting efficiency gain.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, pipeline equations, and constant-call-complexity argument are retained. The Information Bottleneck passage is clarified as conceptual inspiration; no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The collaborative-memory contribution, architectural decoupling, and four-benchmark performance claims remain. v3 explicitly emphasizes benefits for data-sparse users and qualifies the efficiency frontier in Section 3.4 and the conclusion as concerning online inference cost.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new results as compensating for sparse histories and buffering noisy interactions. Appendix G.2 additionally interprets retained low-overlap peers as semantically useful diversity. The cost discussion distinguishes offline memory work from online serving, while the dedicated limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G.2 newly specifies that the generic-rule control equally weights normalized features. Table 5 separates online and complete-session token usage and clarifies local memory-maintenance costs. Model deployments, hardware, hyperparameters, complete prompts, and access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references concerning H-Mem, dynamic graph retrieval, adaptive negative sampling, fairness, and unlabeled-data recommendation. Appendix B.2 adds a connection to user-side fairness and long-tail recommendation, while retaining the original collaborative-memory positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, motivation passages, cost discussion, and conclusion are revised, and Appendix F descriptions are shortened. Further analyses are grouped under a new RQ5 subsection, acknowledgements are added, and the contents page is removed. The principal section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds three boxed method illustrations, two robustness plots, and Table 11. It redraws the cost frontier and expands Table 5's token-accounting display. Much appendix prose changes from single-column to two-column layout, with tables and figures relocated; existing prompt and case-study figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful robustness and curation evidence and clearer method illustrations, but introduces an inconsistency in the central efficiency evidence. In v1, Table 8's stages sum to its approximately 9,700-token total; in v3, they sum to approximately 5,325, not the reported 6,400. The added evidence and reduced numerical reliability have competing effects, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
